articles.headline: US accuses Chinese AI firms of malicious copying of AI technology
articles.summary: The dispute adds to geopolitical and supply-chain risk around frontier AI development, especially for firms with exposure to China, cross-border research, or AI model supply chains. Businesses should factor in tighter scrutiny, potential sanctions pressure, and rising compliance costs when sourcing or partnering in AI.

articles.headline: German military evaluating 30 AI tools for use from 2027
articles.summary: The evaluation of 30 AI tools signals growing institutional demand for enterprise-grade AI in regulated, mission-critical settings. Vendors serving government and large organizations may see new procurement opportunities, but also higher compliance and security requirements.

articles.headline: Major AI firms agree to Ottawa’s new data-centre framework
articles.summary: Canada’s new framework for data-centre development affects where AI infrastructure can be built and how public opposition is managed. That matters for enterprises planning cloud capacity, regional resilience, and long-term infrastructure costs.
